subject: Dedicated capacity definitions and SLA / service-credit redlines — Halo Insurance
messages:
From: JP Ramos <jp.ramos@haloinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@haloinc.com>, contracts@haloinc.com
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on Dedicated capacity defs + remedy language

Marissa — thanks again for the demo last week. Were close on internal budget, but our procurement and legal teams flagged two items in the draft: 1) the definition of what counts as a "capacity unit" and how throughput is measured for purposes of the SLA, and 2) the service-credit calculation and cap under Section 7 (SLA remedies).

Short list of asks so we can move forward:
- Can you confirm exactly what one Dedicated Capacity Unit (DCU) represents? Is it a single A100 80GB-equivalent GPU, or some pooled vGPU measure? We need a deterministic mapping so our architects can size the pool.
- How will throughput be measured (tokens/sec, concurrent streams, or requests/minute) and which measurement windows apply for SLA breach determination?
- Our legal is pushing to increase the service-credit cap to 50% of monthly fees for sustained breaches — can you explain Redwoods rationale and whether theres flexibility (we have a 36-month commit request).

Attached are the redline excerpts from our counsel. Please loop in finance/legal on Redwood's side. Wed like to close pricing and move the redlines next week.

Thanks,
JP
VP, Platform Engineering
Halo Insurance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated capacity defs + remedy language

JP — thanks for the clear list. Ive summarized Redwoods position below and attached an updated draft (Draft_Commit_Terms_v3.docx) that includes proposed language for DCU and our standard SLA calculation. High level:

1) Definition: Dedicated Capacity Unit (DCU) \u2014 one DCU = physical slot equivalent to an NVIDIA A100 80GB (or rail-equivalent on other supported hardware). For pooled clusters we express capacity as DCUs (integer count) and map to GPUs via an internal equivalence table in Appendix A. This gives a deterministic sizing input for your architects.

2) Throughput measurement: We measure "throughput" for SLA purposes as successful inference completions per minute, normalized to a 512-token sequence length and a baseline model profile. Operationally we use a rolling 1-hour window sampled in 5-minute intervals and require at least 95% of minute-level samples to meet the throughput target to avoid a breach. We also capture per-request latency percentiles for diagnostics. See Throughput_Benchmark.xlsx for typical DCU throughput numbers at different sequence lengths.

3) Service credits & cap: Redwoods standard is a graduated credit (5%-20% of monthly committed fee) depending on severity and outage duration, with a 20% monthly cap and 50% quarterly cap for repeated breaches. The cap exists to keep credits proportional and not interfere with recovery/mitigation incentives.

That said, given the size of your commit and the multi-year term, were prepared to negotiate an elevated quarterly cap (up to 35%) subject to a mutually-agreed traffic profile and an SLA measurement playbook. We cannot accept an unconditional 50% monthly credit.

Next steps: Ill review the HALO_SLA_redlines with Laura (legal) and Vivek (finance) and send back a marked draft by EOD Tue 9 Jun. If youre ok with the DCU mapping approach and measurement windows, please flag any model-profiles we should include as "baseline" for the first 12 months.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated capacity defs + remedy language

Looping in some bench numbers to make the DCU mapping concrete. In our internal benchmarks (see attached Throughput_Benchmark.xlsx):
- A single DCU (A100-80GB equivalent) delivers ~1,900 tokens/sec for an OPT-style decoder with 512 token sequences when serving with our continuous batching + KV-cache.
- For chat-style workloads (short-turn, 64-128 tokens) the effective per-DCU throughput increases ~2.5x due to shorter sequences and batching efficiency.
- Were happy to provide an initial baseline run using one of Halos representative prompts to lock the model profile used for SLA measurement.

Technical note: because latency and throughput vary with sequence distribution, the measurement playbook must include the baseline prompt set, traffic weighting, and a sampling window. Without that, any flat monthly credit cap is hard to correlate to actual degradation.

-rishi
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Halo redlines to SLA remedies (excerpt)

Marissa / Laura — please see excerpted redlines below (weve removed unrelated clauses). Our counsel proposes: 
- Replace Redwoods 20% monthly cap with a 50% monthly cap for any calendar month with a sustained SLA breach (sustained defined as >6 hours cumulative in a 24-hour period).
- Add an automatic termination right if monthly credits exceed 70% of monthly committed fees for two consecutive months.

Were open to a playbook for measurement but cannot accept a solution where service credits are always immaterial. Given our regulatory exposure, we need stronger remediation spelled out.

-can you confirm Redwoods ability to accept a higher cap if we push for higher discounts?

Thanks,
Halo Insurance Legal Team
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: contracts@haloinc.com, JP Ramos <jp.ramos@haloinc.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Halo redlines to SLA remedies (excerpt)

Thanks — I pulled finance and legal into a short proposal to bridge the gap. Our suggested compromise for the contract redline: 

1) Monthly cap: increase from standard 20% to 30% (of monthly committed fees) for the first twelve months of the committed term, provided Halo commits to a minimum 24-month reserved commit at the agreed pricing tier.

2) Quarterly cap: up to 45% (not to exceed 45% per quarter) for repeated breaches, measured on a rolling 90-day window.

3) Sustained breach definition: >6 hours cumulative degraded throughput within a 24-hour window, as measured by the mutually-agreed measurement playbook (baseline prompt set + sampling intervals).

4) Termination right: in lieu of full termination, allow an escalated remediation path: if credits exceed 45% in two consecutive months, both parties enter a 30-day remediation and root-cause process. If unresolved, Halo may request early termination with a shortened exit period and an agreed deprovisioning timeline. Were reluctant to accept an immediate termination for credits alone without an opportunity to remediate.

5) Discount flexibility: Vivek can offer an additional 7% one-time upfront discount on the committed capacity if Halo accepts our proposed caps and commits to a 36-month term with prepayment terms.

If this is acceptable in principle Ill send a marked doc and a tracked change set for your counsel. Otherwise we can schedule a 30-minute call Thurs morning to work through live redlines.

Best,
Marissa

Team — internal next steps before I send the marked draft back to Halo: 
- Laura: please review the proposed compromise language on termination and the 30-day remediation step. Legal should confirm the wording around "mutually-agreed measurement playbook" and what happens if parties cannot agree on the baseline profile. Can we include an arbitration tie-breaker (e.g., neutral third-party measurement) if measurement disputes persist?
- Vivek: confirm whether the 7% one-time prepay discount is good to offer and whether it affects revenue recognition obligations. Also confirm the financial impact of bumping the monthly cap to 30% in the first year.
- Rishi: can you prepare a quick, signed-off baseline run using Halos sample prompts once JP sends them (Ill request this). We need that artifact to include as an appendix to the SLA.

Goal: respond to Halos counsel with the marked draft by EOD Thu 11 Jun. If Halo pushes back on the 30%/45% compromise, we keep the call on Thurs to resolve.

-Marissa
Account Executive
